decision: Build approach D: a first-class Tiller.Mutation vocabulary across 5 axes (whitelist, result override, driver swap, injected latency, process kill), N-way concurrent fork race under DynamicSupervisor, LiveView inspector, and automatic first-divergence plus smallest-decisive-mutation analysis.
rationale: Chosen over C (single whitelist axis, recommended), A (vertical slice), B (event core first). Effort XL, risk High, accepted knowingly. Only version that makes the screen an instrument rather than a spectacle. Foundation is 250-400 lines (revised up from a 30-line estimate after Codex verified spawn_subagent blocks at actions.ex:52): cast-based session loop, attributed ordered event store replacing the global list, Phoenix.PubSub, Replay driver with recorded-result injection. Documented fallback to approach C if the 30-minute divergence-detection spike fails.

decision: Rank 'smallest decisive mutation' by effect on the trajectory: decisive = different ending; smallest = fewest differing turns, later divergence, then within-axis size. No cross-axis weights.
rationale: Open Question 3. Weights are arbitrary and within-axis-only ranking gives no winner. Measuring the trajectory (Tiller.Divergence.distance/2) uses what the log already has and needs no scale across axes.

decision: Lay out many branches as a branch-by-turn grid ranked by Tiller.Race, with a card for the picked branch, instead of a card per branch.
rationale: Open Question 4. Cards stop being an instrument past about eight branches; a grid of coloured cells shows divergence points for 32 branches on one screen and doubles as a turn selector.

decision: Make kill_at a resume: snapshots in Tiller.State, branch tool state unlinked under Tiller.ToolStates, restart resumes at the in-flight turn. The tool runs before the kill and again after, so the log shows it once and the world twice.
rationale: Open Question 5. A supervisor restart from initial args is a duplicate, not a counterfactual. With per-turn snapshots already in the store the resume is cheap, and re-running the in-flight turn is the honest at-least-once behaviour of supervised agents.

decision: Integrate tiller with open-seed as an MCP client of the engine (option 1): Tiller.Seed speaks JSON-RPC to `seed mcp serve`, Tiller.Tools gains seed_* port verbs, root sessions hold the worker verbs and subagents only the reads; operator verbs are on no whitelist. Options 2 (tiller as a seed-harness adapter), 3 (tiller as Seed's trajectory instrument), and 4 (open-seed as tiller's template) are recorded in docs/designs/open-seed-integration.md and deferred.
rationale: Needs no LLM driver, respects open-seed's rule that only the port touches a store, and gives tiller real tools with distinct failure modes (the port's exit classes: 2 contention, 3 invalid transition, 6 fenced out) which the butterfly lab lists as its next step. Option 2 is blocked on a real driver (FakeDriver would duplicate scripts/harness/mock); option 3 on the async/attributed event core plus persistence; option 4 only pays off with multiple agents on tiller.

decision: LLM driver defaults to claude-opus-5, effort low, raw HTTP via :httpc and built-in JSON; no new dependency in lib/tiller.
rationale: Adaptive thinking on by default, every tool_choice accepted, no classifier refusals to route around. Elixir has no official SDK and the lab must run in web sessions with no credential, so tests use a scripted Messages API stand-in on the existing Bandit dependency.

decision: The first LLM-driven task is the toy world (put/get/spend/flaky/sleep); the open-seed loop is second.
rationale: No external process, fully testable against the fake API, every mutation axis applies. Branch isolation stops at the seed engine, which is a fixture problem to solve separately.

decision: Runs end with a done/1 tool; a plain text reply is treated as done(text). Drivers gain optional observe/3 and override/3 callbacks and may halt with a reason.
rationale: The final answer becomes an action in the log so Tiller.Race compares outcomes on it. observe/3 is how a result reaches a driver at all; override/3 lets a result-override fork edit the conversation and strip later thinking blocks, which the API requires for an edited history.

decision: The LLM driver MVP is built to docs/designs/llm-driver.md: Wire + Tools.Schema, done/1, observe/3 and override/3 on Tiller.Driver, {:halt, reason}, Tiller.Driver.LLM over :httpc, and Tiller.FakeMessages as the Plug the suite tests against. One correction to the design: the request's tools array is derived per request from Tiller.Session.current_whitelist/0 rather than baked into the driver context at creation.
rationale: A baked tools array would leave a {:whitelist, list} branch's model still offered a tool the session would refuse, which contradicts the design's own claim that a whitelist mutation is literally a different tools array. Deriving it from the session the driver runs inside makes the capability boundary and the prompt the same object, and a test asserts the branch plans without the tool instead of being refused after choosing it.
